messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been observed and confirmed so far is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (about 200,000 km). Its mass is estimated to be around 10–20 Jupiter masses, making it one of the most massive “super‑Jupiter” planets known.

In our own Solar System, the biggest planet is **Jupiter**, which has a radius of about 71,500 km (≈11.2 Earth radii) and a mass of 1.9 × 10²⁷ kg. Beyond that, astronomers continue to discover increasingly massive exoplanets, but none have yet surpassed HD 100546 b in size.
